chapters.title: What's in a Name?
chapters.summary: In this chapter: lesson 1: keeping track of cows; lesson 2: animals and their names; lesson 3: names and number names; lesson 4: puzzles with number names.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Keeping Track of Cows

activities.prompt: How could we keep track of every cow?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Using Marks to Track Cows
activities.body: Deba and Deep took their cows out for grazing, or eating grass, every day. They did not know how to count. Their friend suggested making one mark for each cow leaving the gate. They struck out a mark whenever a cow came back. This system worked the next day. Later, two marks remained although no cows were outside. They found the missing cows nearby.
keyPoints: Make a mark when each cow leaves.
Strike out a mark when each cow returns.
Remaining marks help show that cows are missing.
activities.explanation: Good job listening to how the marks helped.

activities.prompt: Deba made 10 marks when cows left the gate and struck out 3 marks when cows came back. How many cows are still outside?
steps: There were 10 marks made when the cows left.
Striking out 3 marks shows that 3 cows came back.
The marks left are 10 - 3 = 7 cows.

gen.template: Deba made {a} marks when cows left the gate and struck out {b} marks when cows came back. How many cows are still outside?
steps: There were {a} marks made when the cows left.
Striking out {b} marks shows that {b} cows came back.
The marks left are {a} - {b} = {answer} cows.
gen.hint: Count the marks that were not struck out.

activities.explanation: Watch how it is solved.

activities.prompt: Deba and Deep cannot count. How can they keep track of their cows?
steps: They used marks because they could not count.
They made a mark for each cow leaving the gate.
They struck out a mark whenever a cow came back.
Every mark was crossed out, so all their cows had returned.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.prompt: What did their friend suggest?
options: Make a mark for each cow.
Count the cows leaving.
Call each cow by a name.
Watch the cows from home.
activities.explanation: Their friend suggested making one mark for every cow leaving the gate.

activities.prompt: Deba and Deep knew how to count before using marks.
activities.explanation: They did not know how to count, so they used marks instead.

activities.prompt: A wall has 7 cow marks, and 3 of them have been struck out. How many marks remain on the wall?
activities.explanation: The wall has 7 marks in total. 3 marks have been struck out. The remaining marks are 7 - 3 = 4 marks.
steps: The wall has 7 marks in total.
3 marks have been struck out.
The remaining marks are 7 - 3 = 4 marks.
activities.hint: Subtract the struck-out marks from all the marks.

steps: The wall has {a} marks in total.
{b} marks have been struck out.
The remaining marks are {a} - {b} = {answer} marks.
gen.hint: Subtract the struck-out marks from all the marks.

activities.prompt: The cows made 12 marks as they went out, and 7 marks were struck out as they returned. How many cows did not come back?
activities.explanation: There are 12 outgoing marks. The 7 struck-out marks show cows that came back. The cows that did not come back are 12 - 7 = 5 cows.
steps: There are 12 outgoing marks.
The 7 struck-out marks show cows that came back.
The cows that did not come back are 12 - 7 = 5 cows.
activities.hint: Only the marks that were not struck out show missing cows.

gen.hint: Only the marks that were not struck out show missing cows.

activities.prompt: Match each action with what happened.
activities.explanation: Each cow had a mark, and that mark was struck out when it returned.

activities.prompt: At a laddoo shop, the worker made one mark for every tray of laddoos taken out and struck out a mark for every tray brought back. If 9 trays went out and 6 came back, how many tray marks remain?
activities.explanation: The worker made 9 marks for the trays taken out. 6 marks were struck out for the trays brought back. The marks that remain show 9 - 6 = 3 trays.
steps: The worker made 9 marks for the trays taken out.
6 marks were struck out for the trays brought back.
The marks that remain show 9 - 6 = 3 trays.
activities.hint: Take the returned trays away from the trays that went out.

activities.explanation: There are 14 marks for the marbles put into the bag. Taking out 6 marbles strikes out 6 marks. The marbles still in the bag are 14 - 6 = 8 marbles.
steps: There are 14 marks for the marbles put into the bag.
Taking out 6 marbles strikes out 6 marks.
The marbles still in the bag are 14 - 6 = 8 marbles.
activities.hint: Count the marks left after the marbles taken out are marked off.

activities.explanation: There are 12 marks for the children who entered. The marks for 4 leaving children were struck out. The children still in the playground are 12 - 4 = 8 children.
steps: There are 12 marks for the children who entered.
The marks for 4 leaving children were struck out.
The children still in the playground are 12 - 4 = 8 children.

activities.explanation: The worker made 11 marks for the coins taken out. 9 marks were struck out when coins were put back. The coins still missing are 11 - 9 = 2 coins.
steps: The worker made 11 marks for the coins taken out.
9 marks were struck out when coins were put back.
The coins still missing are 11 - 9 = 2 coins.
activities.hint: The remaining marks show the coins that did not come back.

activities.prompt: For a cricket practice game, one mark was made for every ball sent to the field and one mark was struck out for every ball returned. If 12 balls went out and 3 came back, how many balls are still outside?
activities.explanation: There are 12 marks for the balls sent to the field. 3 marks were struck out for the balls that returned. The balls still outside are 12 - 3 = 9 balls.
steps: There are 12 marks for the balls sent to the field.
3 marks were struck out for the balls that returned.
The balls still outside are 12 - 3 = 9 balls.
activities.hint: Subtract the returned balls from the balls sent out.

activities.prompt: Put the cow-marking events in order.
items: They follow the idea the next day
Each cow leaving gets a mark
Each returning cow has its mark struck out
They come home with every mark struck out
activities.explanation: They followed the idea, marked leaving cows, and struck out marks for returning cows.

activities.prompt: A family makes a mark for each cow leaving a gate. No marks are crossed out. What does this show?
options: No cow has come back through the gate.
Every cow has come back through the gate.
No cow left through the gate at all.
Some cows have already come back home.

why.Every cow has come back through the gate: This swaps the leaving marks with the returning marks.
It mistakes un-crossed marks for marks that were never made.
Crossed-out marks show cows that have already returned.

activities.explanation: Each un-crossed mark means that cow has not returned through the gate.

activities.prompt: A family makes marks for cows leaving. It forgets to cross out returning cows. What will the wall show?
options: Many marks will remain after all the cows return.
No marks will remain after all the cows return.
Only marks for cows that never left will remain.
Every mark will be crossed out after the cows return.

why.No marks will remain after all the cows: It assumes returning cows cross out their own marks.
why.Only marks for cows that never left will: It forgets that every leaving cow was given a mark.
why.Every mark will be crossed out after the: It assumes a return crosses out a mark without being told.

activities.explanation: Cows that returned did not have their marks crossed out.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Animals and Their Names

activities.prompt: Can we find the longest and shortest animal names together?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Track Animals and Compare Names
activities.body: Hemant has 36 cows and 23 sheep. He can track his animals using marks. The teacher suggests counting large groups without numbers. Some animals and birds join a game and make two teams. The first captain has the longest name. The second has the shortest. Children can mark the shortest and longest names. They can also share their counting strategies.
keyPoints: Hemant keeps track with marks.
Captains show longest and shortest names.
Children share counting strategies.
activities.explanation: These ideas help you count animals and compare names.

activities.prompt: Hemant has 5 cows and 6 sheep. If he makes one mark for each animal, how many animal marks will he have?
steps: Hemant has 5 cows and 6 sheep.
Mark and count all the cows and sheep together: 11 animals.
5 + 6 = 11 animal marks.

gen.template: Hemant has {cows} cows and {sheep} sheep. If he makes one mark for each animal, how many animal marks will he have?
steps: Hemant has {cows} cows and {sheep} sheep.
Mark and count all the cows and sheep together: {total} animals.
{cows} + {sheep} = {answer} animal marks.
gen.hint: Make one mark for each cow and each sheep.

activities.explanation: Watch how it is solved.

activities.prompt: Hemant had ______ cows.
activities.hint: Think about the number of cows Hemant had.
activities.explanation: Great choice! Hemant uses marks to keep track of his animals.

activities.prompt: Which animal name has the fewest letters?
options: ox
dog
tiger
elephant
activities.explanation: Ox has the fewest letters in this group. You compared each name carefully!
derived: dog has 3 letters = d + o + g
tiger has 5 letters = t + i + g + e + r
elephant has 8 letters = e + l + e + p + h + a + n + t

activities.prompt: The first team has 10 animals and the second team has 8 animals. How many more animals does the larger team have?
activities.explanation: The first team has 10 animals and the second team has 8 animals. Since 10 is greater than 8, subtract the smaller count from the larger count: 2 animals. 10 - 8 = 2 animals.
steps: The first team has 10 animals and the second team has 8 animals.
Since 10 is greater than 8, subtract the smaller count from the larger count: 2 animals.
10 - 8 = 2 animals.
activities.hint: Compare the two team counts before finding the difference.

{a} - {b} = {answer} animals.

steps: The longest name has 8 letters and the shortest name has 6 letters.

8 - 6 = 2 letters.
activities.hint: Compare the number of letters in the two names.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Names and Number Names

activities.prompt: Can you discover which letter begins the most names in your class?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: Names and Number Names
activities.body: Write the names of some friends. Find the shortest and longest names. Write the starting letter of your name. Count names with the same starting letter. Find the most used starting letter and count those names. Count names with the same ending letter. Find letters that do not start any name. Number cards can make roll numbers. The number name of 43 has 10 letters.
keyPoints: Names can be compared by length.
Starting and ending letters help us group names.
Number cards can help us make roll numbers.
activities.explanation: These tasks help you study names and read number names.

activities.prompt: Teji and Jojo have friends' names on a list. How can they find the shortest and longest names?
steps: Teji and Jojo look at their friends' names.
They count letters because shortest names have the fewest letters.
They compare totals because longest names have the most letters.
They also compare starting-letter totals to find the most used letter.
activities.explanation: Think it through with Hooty.

activities.title: The Names Task
activities.prompt: What are you asked to write down?
options: your friends' names
your school timetable
your favourite games
your daily lessons
activities.explanation: The names task asks you to write down some friends' names.

activities.title: Teji's Roll Number
activities.prompt: Teji makes her roll number ______ using number cards.
activities.hint: Use the roll number made by Teji.
activities.explanation: Teji makes her roll number 43 using number cards.

activities.title: Letters in a Number Name
activities.prompt: The number name of 43 has ______ letters.
activities.hint: Think about the written number name.
activities.explanation: The number name of 43 has 10 letters.

activities.title: Shortest Names
activities.prompt: The names task includes finding the shortest names.
activities.explanation: Yes, finding the shortest names is one part of this task.

activities.title: Match the Names Tasks
activities.prompt: Match each names task to its result.
activities.explanation: Each task has a clear result connected to the names.

activities.title: Roll Numbers
activities.prompt: Teji and Jojo make roll numbers with number cards. Which statement is true?
options: Teji's roll number is 43.
Teji's roll number is 17.
Jojo's roll number is 43.
Jojo's roll number is 10.
activities.explanation: Teji makes 43, while Jojo makes 17 using number cards.

activities.prompt: Teji says counting first letters will find the shortest names. What should she do instead?
options: Count the first letter of each name again
Count the letters in each name
Count the last letter of each name
Count how many names are on the list

why.Count the first letter of each name agai: This confuses the first letter with the whole name length.
why.Count the last letter of each name: This confuses the last letter with the whole name length.
why.Count how many names are on the list: This counts how many names there are, not their lengths.

activities.explanation: Counting all letters compares the full length of each name.

activities.prompt: Children write each friend's name on a class list. How can they find the most used starting letter?
options: Choose the first letter on the list
Choose the longest name on the list
Tally each first letter and compare totals
Tally each last letter and compare totals

why.Choose the first letter on the list: The first name may not use the most common letter.
why.Choose the longest name on the list: The longest name does not show the most used starting letter.
why.Tally each last letter and compare total: This confuses ending letters with starting letters.

activities.explanation: Tallying first letters shows which starting letter is used most.

activities.prompt: Jojo is checking which names end with the same letter as his. What should he compare?
options: The number of letters in every name
The first letter of every name
The number cards under every name
The last letter of every name

why.The number of letters in every name: Name length does not show which names share an ending.
why.The first letter of every name: This confuses starting letters with ending letters.
why.The number cards under every name: Number cards cannot show the ending letter of a name.

activities.explanation: Matching last letters finds names with the same ending letter.

activities.prompt: Teji made 43 with number cards. How can she check the length of its number name?
options: Count the number cards she used
Count the first letters of the names
Count the letters in the number name
Count the friend names on the list

why.Count the number cards she used: Number cards build the number, not the words for its name.
why.Count the first letters of the names: Starting letters belong to the friends' names task.
why.Count the friend names on the list: Friend names are not the number name of 43.

activities.explanation: Counting its number-name letters checks the length asked for.

activities.title: Number Name Puzzles
activities.body: Number names can be puzzles. The number 56 is called fifty-six, and its name has 8 letters. Children look for other numbers from 1 to 99 with 8-letter names. They also find numbers with the longest names. One puzzle uses two words: 6 letters and 5 letters. Another uses 63 to 78. Venkatanarasimharajuvaripeta is an Indian place with the longest name.
keyPoints: The number 56 is called fifty-six and has 8 letters.
One number name has two words with 6 and 5 letters.
Venkatanarasimharajuvaripeta has the longest place name.

activities.title: Different ways to sort

Children look for what is common in Jojo's groups. Later, they sort pictures of household objects. They write object names into two groups. One group needs electricity. The other does not. They group the objects differently.

chapters.summary: In this chapter: how people began to count; making one hundred; writing numbers above one hundred; claps, snaps and pats.

lessons.title: How People Began to Count

activities.prompt: How did people first learn to count the things around them?
activities.explanation: Now read on to find out.

activities.title: From Marks to Numbers
activities.body: Long ago, people began counting and kept records with marks. They made marks on cave walls and tree bark. They grouped records in fives, tens, twenties and sixties. Ancient Indians made a method for writing any number. It uses ten symbols, including 0. The symbol 0 means nothing. It made the numeral system work. The method is now used everywhere in the world.
keyPoints: People made marks on cave walls and tree bark.
The number method uses ten symbols.
Zero means nothing and makes the numeral system work.
activities.explanation: Notice the early marks, the ten symbols and the important role of 0.

activities.context: Tens of thousands of years ago, people began counting. They made marks on cave walls and tree bark. They grouped records in fives, tens, twenties and sixties. Ancient Indians made a ten-symbol method for writing any number. The symbol ‘0’ means nothing or the absence of something, and number zero made the numeral system work. It made possible the invention of TVs and computers. It helped make mobile phones possible and is now used everywhere in the world.
activities.prompt: If the symbol ‘0’ were removed from the number-writing method, what would happen?

People could still group records in fives.
The method would become easier to use.
TVs and computers would still be invented in the same way.

why.People could still group records in five: Grouping records does not replace the numeral system.
Removing a needed symbol would not simplify the method.
why.TVs and computers would still be invente: The method helped make these inventions possible.

activities.explanation: Zero makes the numeral system work.
